title: A bounded-below torsion-cohomology object has a torsion-sheaf complex representative
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be any small site in the universe convention [def-weil-size-convention], and let $\operatorname{Ab}(\mathcal C)$ be its category of abelian sheaves [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology]. Call an abelian sheaf torsion if, for every section $s\in F(U)$, there is a covering $\{U_i\to U\}$ and positive integers $n_i$ with $n_i s|_{U_i}=0$. Let $K\in D^+(\operatorname{Ab}(\mathcal C))$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], where $D^+$ consists of derived objects whose cohomology is zero in all sufficiently negative degrees. Suppose each $H^r(K)$ is torsion. There are an integer $a$, a cochain complex $L^\bullet$ of abelian sheaves with $L^r=0$ for $r<a$ and every $L^r$ torsion, and an isomorphism $Q(L^\bullet)\simeq K$ in $D(\operatorname{Ab}(\mathcal C))$, where $Q$ is localization at quasi-isomorphisms. No common annihilator for the terms or for the cohomology sheaves is required.

source.place: Tag 0DD7, lemma-torsion, bounded-below consequence used explicitly in etale-cohomology.tex Tag 0DE5, lemma-cohomological-descent-etale-ph, first paragraph.

proof.text: Since $K\in D^+$, choose an integer $a$ with $H^r(K)=0$ for all $r<a$. By [lem-weil-pbc-site-sheaves-enough-injectives], $\operatorname{Ab}(\mathcal C)$ is an abelian category with enough injectives, and $K$ lies in its bounded below derived category (the cohomology condition defining $D^+$ in the item is that of [lem-weil-pbc-dplus-injective-representative]). Clause (1) of [lem-weil-pbc-dplus-injective-representative] with $n=a$ gives a cochain complex $I^\bullet$ of injective abelian sheaves with $I^r=0$ for $r<a$ and an isomorphism $Q(I^\bullet)\simeq K$. Since $H^r\circ Q\cong H^r$, every cohomology sheaf $H^r(I^\bullet)\cong H^r(K)$ is torsion by hypothesis.

source.place: Tag 0DD7, lemma-torsion, proof: choose an injective representative; bounded-below consequence used in etale-cohomology.tex Tag 0DE5, lemma-cohomological-descent-etale-ph, first paragraph.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-torsion-injective-subcomplex] to $I^\bullet$: with $L^r=I^r_{\mathrm{tor}}\subseteq I^r$ the subsheaf of sections locally annihilated by positive integers, the differentials of $I^\bullet$ preserve these subsheaves (if $n_is|_{U_i}=0$ then $n_i\,d(s)|_{U_i}=0$), and the inclusion $L^\bullet\hookrightarrow I^\bullet$ is a quasi-isomorphism. Each $L^r$ is torsion in the sense of the statement by its definition, and $L^r=0$ for $r<a$ because $I^r=0$ there. Localization inverts quasi-isomorphisms, so $Q(L^\bullet)\simeq Q(I^\bullet)\simeq K$. No common annihilator is chosen anywhere: the integer $n_i$ depends on the section and on the covering member.

source.place: Tag 0DD7, lemma-torsion, proof: the claim that $\mathcal I^\bullet_{tor}\to\mathcal I^\bullet$ is a quasi-isomorphism for a complex of injectives with torsion cohomology.

It keeps local torsion with no common annihilator and is not weakened; small cases (K=0, Q/Z[0], shifts, the empty site) check out. I dropped the node and its only citation. (3) B3/C4: lem-trf-torsion-injective-subcomplex said its torsion condition came from def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology, which does not define torsion. It also carried an unused stmt_dep, def-weil-pbc-kinjective-resolutions. I now define torsion inline and removed that stmt_dep. reviewed_lean.note: The Lean statement matches lem-trf-torsion-sheaf-complex-representative clause by clause, with the node's quantifier order. The site is J.IsSiteForCoverings with independent universes u and v, and coefficients are AddCommGrpCat.{max u v t}. hK is the node's cohomological D+ bound and the conclusion's bound is termwise. Every cohomology sheaf and every term of L is torsion, using the existing upstream Sheaf.IsTorsion (covering sieve, IsOfFinAddOrder), which is equivalent to the node's covering-family definition under IsSiteForCoverings. Edge cases checked: K=0, Q/Z in any degree, orders varying by component, negative degrees, the empty site and the empty cover. No duplicate declaration found.
